source.title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds

accepted.question_text: Suppose a sequence of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space (X, d, p), with Ric_i ≥ −λ and a noncollapsing lower volume bound Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. Is the limit space X bi-Lipschitz to a manifold outside a singular subset of codimension two?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.2. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Rici ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then is X bi-Lipschitz to a manifold away from a set of codimension two?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a sequence of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space (X, d, p), with Ric_i ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. Is X homeomorphic to a manifold outside a singular subset of codimension three?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.4. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Rici ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then X is homeomorphic to a manifold away from a set of codimension three.

accepted.question_text: Suppose a sequence of pointed n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space (X, d, p), with Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. Is it true that, outside a subset of codimension three in X, each point has a unique tangent cone?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.7. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then the tangent cones of X are unique away from a set of codimension three.

accepted.question_text: Suppose a sequence of pointed n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space (X, d, p), with Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For a fixed point x in X, are all tangent cones at x homeomorphic to one another outside a subset of codimension five?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.9. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then the tangent cones of X are all homoemorphic at a fixed point away from a set of codimension five.

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d, p) be a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit obtained as a Gromov–Hausdorff limit of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For the Federer stratification S^k(X) = {x ∈ X : no tangent cone at x is (k+1)-symmetric}, is S^k(X) contained in a union of k-dimensional submanifolds in the following sense: there exists a countable collection of bi-Hölder maps φ_i : B_1(0^k) → M such that, if Ŝ^k(X) = ⋃_i φ_i(B_1(0^k)), then S^k(X) ⊆ Ŝ^k(X) and every tangent cone at each x ∈ Ŝ^k(X) is at least k-symmetric?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.11 (stratification). We define the k-stratum Sk(X) ⊆ X by Sk(X) ≡ {x ∈ X : no tangent cone at x is k + 1-symmetric}.

Conjecture 2.15. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then Sk is contained in a union of k-dimensional submanifolds. More precisely, there exist a countable collection of bi-Hölder maps ϕi : B1(0k) → M such that if Ŝk(X) ≡ ⋃i ϕi(B1(0k)) then 1) Sk(X) ⊆ Ŝk(X), 2) for each x ∈ Ŝk(X) we have that every tangent cone is at least k-symmetric.

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d, p) be a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit obtained as a Gromov–Hausdorff limit of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For each k ≤ n − 2, does there exist a subset Ŝ^k of Hausdorff dimension at most k such that every point x ∈ X \ Ŝ^k has the property that every tangent cone at x is at least (k+1)-symmetric, meaning it splits off at least k+1 Euclidean factors?
accepted.context_brief: refined symmetry away from small set

evidence.quote: We say X is k-symmetric if X ≡ Rk × C(Y ) additionally splits off k-Euclidean factors.

Conjecture 2.16. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then for each k ≤ n − 2 there exists Ŝk with dim Ŝk ≤ k such that for each x ∈ X \ Ŝk we have that every tangent cone is at least k + 1-symmetric.

accepted.question_text: Let (M^n, g, x) be a Riemannian manifold with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(x)) > v > 0. Does there exist a constant C(n, λ, v) such that the scalar curvature has a uniform local L^1 bound ∫_(B_1(x)) R < C?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.18 (noncollapsing Yau’s conjecture). Let Mn, g, x satisfy Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(p)) > v > 0, then ∃ C(n, λ, v) > 0 such that ∫B1(x) R < C.

accepted.question_text: Consider a sequence of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) converging to (X, d, x), with Ric_j ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(x_j)) ≥ v > 0. Let R_j dvol_{g_j} converge as measures on X. On the part of X where tangent cones are uniquely of the form R^(n−2) × C(S^1_{r_x}), with radius function r_x, must the scalar-curvature measures satisfy the energy-identity decomposition R_j dvol_{g_j} → R_X H^n + 2 θ_x H^{n−1}_Σ + 2π(1 − r_x) H^{n−2}_S, where R_X is a locally L^1 function bounded below, Σ is an (n−1)-rectifiable set with θ_x ≤ 1, and the final term is an (n−2)-rectifiable measure supported on the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X)?
accepted.context_brief: energy identity for scalar curvature measures

evidence.quote: To be precise recall from Theorem 2.12 that away from a set of n − 2 measure zero there is a radius function rx such that at any x in the domain we have that the tangent cone at x is unique and isometric to Rn−2 × C(S1rx).

Conjecture 2.20 (energy identity). Let (Mnj, gj, xj) → (X, d, x) satisfy Ricj ≥ −λ and the noncollapsing condition Vol(B1(xj)) ≥ v > 0, then as measures the scalar curvature converges Rj dvj → RXHn + 2θxHn−1Σ + 2π(1 − rx)Hn−2S, where RX : X → R is a locally L1 function which is bounded from below, Σ is an n−1 rectifiable set with θx ≤ 1, and 2π(1−rx)Hn−2S is an n−2-rectifiable measure supported on the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X).

accepted.question_text: Let (M_i^n, g_i, ν_i, p_i) converge in the measured Gromov–Hausdorff sense to (X, d, ν, p), with Ric_i ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) → 0. If Theorem 3.1 gives a unique rectifiable dimension k for X, is the Hausdorff dimension of X equal to this same integer k?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.1 (Cheeger–Colding [2], Colding–Naber [5]). Let Mni, gi, νi, pi → (X, d, ν, p) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) → 0. Then there exists a unique k ≤ n such that X is k-rectifiable.
Open Problem 3.2. Show the Hausdorff dim of X is same as the rectifiable dimension k from Theorem 3.1.

accepted.question_text: Let γ : (−2, 2) → X be a minimizing geodesic in a lower-Ricci limit space. For s, t ∈ (−1, 1), does the normalized volume ratio along γ satisfy a Lipschitz estimate of the form ν(B_r(γ(s))) / ν(B_r(γ(t))) ≤ C(n, λ)|t − s|? In the noncollapsed case, is the infinitesimal density constant along γ in the sense that lim_{r→0} ν(B_r(γ(s))) / ν(B_r(γ(t))) = 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3. Let γ : (−2, 2) → X be a minimizing geodesic, then for s, t ∈ (−1, 1) we have that 1) (Lipschitz rate) ν(Br(γ(s)))/ν(Br(γ(t))) ≤ C(n, λ)|t − s|, 2) (constant density) if X is noncollapsed, then limr→0 ν(Br(γ(s)))/ν(Br(γ(t))) = 1.

accepted.question_text: Suppose a sequence of pointed Riemannian manifolds with normalized measures (M_i^n, g_i, ν_i, p_i) converges in the measured Gromov–Hausdorff sense to (X, d, ν, p), with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) → 0. Does there exist an open subset R(X) ⊆ X of full ν-measure that is homeomorphic to a k-dimensional manifold, where k is the rectifiable dimension of X?
accepted.context_brief: full-measure manifold region in collapsed limits

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.4. Let Mni, gi, νi, pi → (X, d, ν, p) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) → 0, then is there an open subset of full ν-measure R(X) ⊆ X which is homeomorphic to a k-manifold?

accepted.question_text: Let (M^n, g) be a Riemannian manifold with Ric ≥ −λ. Does there exist a constant C(n, λ) such that the scalar curvature satisfies the local bound ∫_(B_1(p)) R ≤ C(n, λ) for every unit ball B_1(p)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5 (local Yau conjecture). Let Mn, g satisfy Ric ≥ −λ, then ∫B1(p) R ≤ C(n, λ).
